Sample: aws-cdk-lib 2.274.0 (AWS Cloud Development Kit library)
SHA256: 66ff7e9120c124930155b0ce8ccabe7482479b6da7b48686431c30f77c29ad66
Verdict: BENIGN

Comparison release: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0, fetched from
https://registry.npmjs.org/aws-cdk-lib/-/aws-cdk-lib-2.273.0.tgz
Both archives match their npm registry SHA512 integrity values.
Manifest/registry provenance is corroboration, not the basis of the verdict.

Decisive diff evidence:
- distributed-map.js, map.js, sqs.js, and user-pool-email.js have identical
  executable logic and imports across these versions. Only their JSII RTTI
  version string changes from 2.273.0 to 2.274.0.
- The reported hidden stage is ../../.warnings.jsii.js (or one additional
  parent level). Its lazy require wrapper caches the imported module. Public
  constructors/methods call its generated validators on their arguments.
- The helper walks argument properties, guards recursive objects with a Set,
  checks deprecated APIs, reads JSII_DEPRECATED, and emits console warnings or
  throws DeprecationError. Its only code change is warning deduplication via
  ALREADY_WARNED and revised warning text. It imports no modules and performs
  no networking, process launch, credential collection, or payload evaluation.
- Map/DistributedMap construct Step Functions state JSON, graph edges, and
  policies. SqsEventSource validates batching/poller options and binds an
  event-source mapping and queue-consumption permissions. UserPoolEmail
  validates sender configuration and builds SES/Cognito settings; its Base64
  operation encodes non-ASCII display names as MIME encoded words.

Package-wide comparison: 6,123 unchanged members, 1,454 changed members,
44 additions, no removals. 1,277 changes are solely the package version.
Other changes include generated AWS resource definitions, model/image/engine
constants, source maps, new AppFabric/Linux-subscription bindings, template
validation/tree/range helpers, and declared dependency upgrades. Manifest
install hooks were not added. fs-extra changes handle dangling symlinks,
cosmetic case/Unicode renames, and directory-emptying behavior.

The EKS handler is an esbuild bundle with ordinary SDK/proxy dependencies.
Exports onEvent/isComplete dispatch CloudFormation Create/Update/Delete events
to EKS/Fargate operations. ResourceProperties.AssumeRoleArn configures the AWS
temporary-credential provider; the configured SDK makes the service requests.
The complete application tail is identical under a consistent bijection of
minified identifiers (3,360 token runs); its bundled dependency code changes
include proxy-code deduplication and IP-address parsing. No additional remote
tasking or credential-export path was identified. Large/minified sources have
reported flow-analysis gaps; manual source/diff review supplied the relevant
call-path evidence. No deployment-specific evidence was supplied.

Trait correction and placement:
- Retire objectives/supply-chain/trojanized/campaign::require-local-stage.
  Its matcher establishes local dotfile module loading, not trojanization.
- Replace it with micro-behaviors/os/module/load::cjs-dotfile-require,
  notable, describing that neutral operation. No attack mapping applies.
  Matcher correction is separate from placement: use a parsed require call
  and its first string argument, require a relative path ending in a dotfile,
  and allow arbitrary directory depth. Comments/quoted code and package
  subpaths no longer count. Ordinary dotfile calls in tests, configurations,
  node_modules, and source remain observable; prior blanket exclusions were
  inappropriate for a neutral capability. No product/name allowlist is used.
- Retire npm-wrapper-hidden-stage: a build-related dependency, a dotfile load,
  and an install hook/clone/domain clue do not require any malicious action
  or modification of legitimate input. There are no consumers of either old
  ID or their ancestor directories, nor broad consumers of the new load leaf.
  This is an intentional removal of an unsupported hostile inference.
- The existing require-from-hidden-path rule matches a hidden directory at
  the start of a path; this rule describes a final dotfile module. They are
  distinct path observations, not duplicate matchers.

Focused controls (run outside testdata to avoid path suppressors): actual
relative dotfile loads in JS/TS and mixed documentation/code stay notable;
ordinary parent paths, package subpaths, hidden-directory-only paths, comments,
and quoted require examples do not match this dotfile rule. All five pass.

Commands: atomscan on the sample before and after edits; cleave facts on the
archive, flagged members, warning helper, and EKS bundle; cleave strings on
the helper (including available decoded string representations); byte and
normalized source diffs; check.py. Scratch holds fetched releases and detailed
facts/diff/scan results outside the traits repository.

Final verification: the sample's full atomscan rescan has zero hostile and
zero suspicious traits across 6,106 reported analysis units. The neutral
dotfile capability remains observable in 1,236 units, including decoded source
layers. The earlier 2.273.0 archive also has no suspicious/hostile findings
under the corrected traits. These results confirm the trait correction; the
behavioral review and decisive version diff establish the BENIGN judgment.
